titleStmt.title: Ovid, Amores 3.4: witness S — first-pass manuscript transcription
titleStmt.author: Publius Ovidius Naso

respStmt.resp: First-pass inspection of every extant verse image and manuscript encoding
respStmt.name: OpenAI Codex, encode_s agent

publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Awaiting independent second source reading; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 389, 390 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 48 extant verse positions were first-read directly from witness S images. Existing annotation rectangles are reproduced without modification. No reading is supplied from LL or another witness. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial. Independent second reading remains required.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. A missing written initial is represented as gap, without inventing its decoration. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.

interpretation.p: Notes are a first-reader evidence queue. Local uncertainty is documentation rather than an automatic user task. A different reader must independently inspect each verse and investigate all notes before integration.

div.head: First-pass encoding notes
div.note: A small D stands well to the left of ure, separated by a conspicuous blank area. The visible small initial and spacing are retained; a planned but absent decorated capital is not asserted. The pale group inposito is locally qualified, and final puelle is preserved.
After ingenio the faint connected group reads provisionally queq; its abbreviated form is not silently expanded to a familiar reading. Final e carries an est suspension mark.
The opening reads Si followed by a q suspension, expanded qua. The barred dempto form is represented as dēpto; repeated casta ē and the denique suspension remain explicit.
The source has Quę qa, not a silently spelled quia. Both n signs are marked; the short marked ending of facit is encoded as a suspension. Word division remains editorial.

The groups before corpus and after it are compressed and pale. The marked bn-like form and adultā-like form are kept as uncertain abbreviations without supplying missing letters. The source reads seruaris and mens; its form is not harmonized with another witness.
The source writes ni without a supplied si. The marked pot form is expanded potest, retaining the visible abbreviation.

The opening abbreviated word is provisionally Omibꝰ, expanded Omnibus at low certainty. The marked form after intus is adult-like but its exact internal letters remain unclear; it is not silently expanded into an expected reading.
The pale word after Semina is provisionally neqūe. Its mark and letters remain locally uncertain and are not reconstructed from a normalized text.
The manuscript writes crede mi and uicia. No h or alternative spelling is supplied.
The raised suspension after apti is encoded with the declared us sign; the line reads ipse tuo.
The contractions nup̄ and equū are retained. The marked contra-like group is provisionally c̄tra, without a forced expansion; the ending of tenacem is suspended.
The final short marked m-like group after ire remains unexpanded and locally unclear. The manuscript image does not securely establish its complete intended word.

The opening reads Nitimur. The marked group following it is provisionally inuetitū; its internal vowel and consonant strokes remain locally qualified. Semper and the que ending are explicit abbreviations, not unstated expansions.
The source has eger and a marked inter- contraction in interdictis; neither is silently regularized.
The et ligature and hūs contraction are retained with expansions; the source writes sępe. A visible point follows Argus.

The pale name is provisionally danaę. After saxo ferroque, a crossed-p form with a marked ending is provisionally Ꝑennē and remains unexpanded. The exact final letters require the independent reader; no complete perenni or other expected form is inserted.
The final group after tradita is pale and disturbed, provisionally mat̄r. Its visible mark remains without a reconstructed complete phrase or an inferred erasure.
The source has contractions for Inter and tam, and a pro suspension before cos. They are retained as visible abbreviations with defensible expansions.

The opening appears Quid with extra crossing strokes and remains locally unclear. Seruat has a suspension; the end of cupim is faint and tentatively represented by the raised us sign. Final furē has a contraction bar and is expanded furem.

The qd group has a crossing stroke and is expanded quod at low certainty. The same marked form at28 receives context-dependent quid and quod expansions; source glyphs remain visible and spacing is editorial.
A short marked s-like group after sua is expanded sed at low certainty. The source has amore mariti, which is retained. The same qualification applies to the short group at29.
Both qd contractions are visible and their expansions remain low certainty. Ceperit and esse putant are retained from the manuscript rather than replaced from another witness.

Proba begins with a pro suspension; quam carries a bar. The short s-like group is qualified, and the marked adultā-like form remains unexpanded. No exact underlying letter sequence or prior correction state is asserted.
The precium contraction is represented schematically as p̄ciū. Corpore and the et-like ending of habet are retained as written.
The contracted form in̄cessa is expanded inconcessa. The visible colon-like stop is retained.
The short group between ingenuam and est is provisionally ius; the joined minims are locally uncertain. Nasal contractions in tamen, ingenuam and puellam remain explicit.
The source uses a raised us sign in metus and e caudata in externę. No other spelling is supplied.
The line has several marked forms: est, nimium, quem and coniunx. The intervening adultā-like abbreviation remains locally qualified and unexpanded. Source ledit is retained.
The compact marked form between martigenę and sine is provisionally n̄s̄, expanded nostri only at low certainty. Its exact displayed minims remain qualified.
Both patronymic forms are provisionally iliades; their initial joined strokes remain locally unclear. The second has an explicit que suspension. No familiar spelling is substituted.

The t with high i is retained as a tibi abbreviation. After formosa a marked sim-like group precedes a conspicuous pale blank and an ut-like group with a separate high i. The uncertain groups, blank spacing and separate inscription are preserved without a supplied missing phrase or asserted deletion.
The dn̄e contraction is expanded domine while retaining the source form; the expansion is not a claim about an independently written ae spelling. The following que sign is explicit.
The opening Grā is a contraction expanded Gratia. Minimo magna labore uenit is retained from the source.
All48 verse positions are present. The next poem begins immediately below this line on the same source page; its text is not incorporated into3.4. The final point is retained.
